jobs.description:
About the client

A large, Brisbane-based education sector organisation found out the hard way what happens when a Salesforce program runs on status updates instead of delivery. An independent health check surfaced the real state of things: broken data models, access that shouldn't exist, integrations that don't talk to each other, and a backlog of work that was reported as done and wasn't. Salesforce professional services is now on-site for 12 months, and this role builds the internal team that works alongside them to actually fix it.
About the role

This isn't a program manager who flourishes a Gantt chart in a steering committee and calls it leadership. The last person in a seat like this one filled governance forums with noise instead of answers, and the organisation is done with that. You'll be the one who reads a health check and sees a plan, not a crisis. You'll run four workstreams (roadmap and governance, platform foundations, data foundations, strategic use cases), and you'll be judged on whether the platform is actually better in twelve months, not on how polished your reporting deck looked along the way. Two business units pull against each other on a shared platform. You'll need to hold that tension without pretending it isn't there.
Duties

Run delivery across all four workstreams to a standard that survives scrutiny, not just a deadline
Build governance reporting that tells executives the truth about risk and progress, not a version of it
Own the program budget and vendor spend, and know exactly where every dollar is going
Earn trust across business units who've been burned before
Spot the risks that turn into fires and deal with them before they do

Requirements

Real experience leading a Salesforce program through actual complexity, not just scale
Multi-cloud depth across Sales, Service, Experience and Marketing Cloud
A program or agile delivery certification that backs up the experience (PMP, PRINCE2 Practitioner, SAFe, CSM or PSM II)
Financial and vendor management you can defend under questioning

Job Summary

Here at the Office for National Statistics (ONS), we have unrivalled access to a vast breadth and depth of data. Every day, we use this to produce trusted statistics and insightful analysis that informs both the public and policymakers on the issues that matter most.

Our work spans the production of essential economic statistics and the analysis that brings them to life to support decision makers and help people understand the UK economy. Our key focus is producing high quality, relevant and timely core statistics: gross domestic product, inflation, public sector finances, labour market statistics, trade and the balance of payments. We're also expanding our use of administrative data, while transforming our surveys and moving off legacy statistical systems.

Following the recent independent review of ONS by Sir Robert Devereux, we’ve launched our Economic Statistics Plan (ESP)—a bold response to restore quality and confidence in our economic statistics. Cloud technologies (Azure, AWS, GCP)

Diversity and inclusion are core DPIRD values. Everyone has the right to contribute and participate to their full potential. We are committed to supporting a diverse and inclusive culture that is respectful, welcoming and flexible – a workplace where our people feel supported, valued, and part of our collective success.

This Role Offers Flexible, People-first Working Conditions, Including

35‑hour base working week
Flexible start and finish times between 6am and 10pm, with core hours of 10am–3pm
Flex time, allowing additional hours worked to be accrued and taken back as flex leave
Generous leave arrangements, including carers’, parental and adoption leave
Four weeks recreation leave as standard.

About The Role

NSW Public Works (NSW PW) is part of the Department of Primary Industries and Regional Development and supports local and state government agencies to deliver critical infrastructure initiatives by providing expert advisory, planning, design, delivery and support services.

We’re seeking an experienced Project Manager to deliver a diverse portfolio of building, and community infrastructure projects across the South Coast. This includes water and wastewater infrastructure, transport interfaces, and public assets critical to regional growth.

You’ll lead projects end-to-end—managing scope, programme, risk, and commercial performance—while acting as a trusted advisor to clients. The role also involves leading procurement and contracts; and supporting a high-performing team environment.

About You

We’re looking for someone with a proven ability to deliver projects in environments where clear communication, good judgement and strong stakeholder engagement are essential.

You Will Bring

A background in architecture, engineering, construction, or major infrastructure project management
Experience managing multiple projects with defined time, cost and quality outcomes across all stages of a project’s lifecycle
Demonstrated experience of design management, contract administration, procurement, and delivery risk management
Strong communication skills with the ability to engage diverse client groups and community stakeholders
A commitment to professional integrity, teamwork, and strong work ethic
Relevant trade, post‑trade or tertiary qualifications (architecture/engineering/ construction/project management)
Demonstrated experience in building, civil, water, wastewater or similar infrastructure
A valid NSW Driver Licence and willingness to travel to project sites across the region (including occasional overnight stays)

This role will suit someone who thrives in a role with variety, autonomy, and a strong client‑service focus.

About Us

NSW Public Works (NSWPW) plays a significant role in the development of our state, our regions, and our infrastructure and associated industries, by supporting local and state government agencies to deliver critical infrastructure initiatives. We do this by providing: expert advisory services; planning, design and delivery management; sustainability, asset management and support services. Our work is in the community facilities, hospitals, dams, water treatment plants, housing and high schools – the real foundations of prosperous communities. Every day we help shape the ambitious projects that bring progress to more people in NSW. From forging a more sustainable relationship with the land around us, to engineering the big ideas of the future. In every challenge we see the chance to build stronger and more connected communities.

Together, we are DPIRD

The New South Wales Department of Primary Industries and Regional Development (DPIRD) protects, supports and develops primary industries and regional economies.

Collectively we support strong and sustainable agriculture, forestry, fishing and mining industries, and regional economies. We actively manage our natural assets: our lands and soils, minerals, waterways and oceans, vegetation and forests.

The department brings together: Local Land Services, NSW Resources, Agriculture and Biosecurity, Fisheries and Forestry, Regional Development and Delivery.

Learn more about the benefits of joining our diverse and talented DPIRD team.

Job Summary

Here at the Office for National Statistics (ONS), we have unrivalled access to a vast breadth and depth of data. Every day, we use this to produce trusted statistics and insightful analysis that informs both the public and policymakers on the issues that matter most.

Our work spans the production of essential economic statistics and the analysis that brings them to life to support decision makers and help people understand the UK economy. Following the recent independent review of ONS by Sir Robert Devereux, we’ve launched our Economic Statistics Plan (ESP)—a bold response to restore quality and confidence in our economic statistics. new_jobs.title: Associate Project Manager - Remote
new_jobs.description:
This role requires the candidate to be located within the Southeast region of the United States.
Will only consider candidates in Alabama, Arkansas, Florida, Georgia, Kentucky, Louisiana, Mississippi, North Carolina, South Carolina, Tennessee and Virginia

Stryker is seeking a tenacious, customer service-focused Associate Project Manager to manage customer engagements from initial transition from Sales through final delivery and transition to the Services team. You will be responsible for delivering high-quality solutions across all care.ai product lines that meet and exceed business and customer satisfaction metrics and satisfy budget and schedule requirements. care.ai specializes in delivering AI-assisted virtual care workflows, smart room technology and ambient intelligence solutions.

What You Will Do

Schedule, facilitate, and lead the transition process from the Sales team to the Services team
Lead the assigned delivery teams to ensure the project meets the scope, schedule, quality and budget expectations
Plan, schedule, and track project milestones, critical paths, deliverables, and accurate revenue forecasting using industry standard tools
Ensure delivery process aligns with standards established through the care.ai Solutions Deployment Methodology
Facilitate project communications, including lead regular project status meetings with all partners, documenting meeting minutes, and managing all ongoing action items
Ensure that all project deliverables and documentation are archived appropriately and in a timely manner, as well as satisfy established project review and audit processes
Conduct project close-out activities, including transitioning processes back to Sales and Support; Elicit, compile, and share post-delivery lessons and feedback
This role requires regular travel, with candidates expected to travel 25% to 50% of the time based on business priorities and customer requirements.

What You Need

Required:

Bachelor’s degree
2+ years of professional experience
Experience with project management software, Monday.com and JIRA preferred

Preferred:

PMP certification
Strong understanding of enterprise network architecture, firewall requirements, and infrastructure components to support secure, scalable business solutions
Healthcare project management experience preferred

Posted Date: 09/02/2026 This role will be posted for a minimum of 3 days.

USN: $69,500 - $110,900 USD Annual

Health benefits include: Medical and prescription drug insurance, dental insurance, vision insurance, critical illness insurance, accident insurance, hospital indemnity insurance, personalized healthcare support, wellbeing program and tobacco cessation program. Financial benefits include: Health Savings Account (HSA), Flexible Spending Accounts (FSAs), 401(k) plan, Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP), basic life and AD&D insurance, and short-term disability insurance. Stryker offers innovative products and services in MedSurg, Neurotechnology, Orthopaedics and Spine that help improve patient and healthcare outcomes. Alongside its customers around the world, Stryker impacts more than 150 million patients annually.
